doc.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025

title: Wide vibrato and out-of-tune pianos
summary: White doubts the theory that wide vibrato came from bad pianos; he says it imitated singing in black churches and blues, and often there was no piano.

story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Yeah, there were some, one of the things I jotted down to talk about was jazz myths. And we can go there, but before I leave Evan, he had this theory about vibrato and that it was, if we listen to Sidney Bechet and others that it was wide partly because they were trying to deal with out of tune pianos.

I don't know about that. I mean I know a lot of older musicians, I know a lot of – I’ve played with more than three dozen musicians born before 1910 and I never heard that. But you know there are a lot of things people – there’s a lot unknown so a lot of times people make up things or they theorize. But you know I think the vibrato is just part of the idea of imitating the singing style that came from black churches and blues, and different singers had different types of vibrato and I think it was just a personal means of expression more than anything else. Because a lot of times when they played here they didn’t have a piano you know.
